comment: The JS -> CSS contract: --dx-* names the runtime sets with style.setProperty and base/** reads. They are not part of the component tier (tests/fluent-next-naming.test.ts excludes them from the surface checks) and their read form is fixed here: `fallback` is the exact text after the comma in var(), null means the read is bare on purpose and `whenUnset` says what happens then. tests/fallback-policy.test.ts holds base/** to this file.

variables.name: --dx-cardview-cardsperrow
variables.whenUnset: the declaration disappears; the runtime always supplies a number (default 3, 'auto' is resolved to a number in view.tsx), so a CSS fallback would only mask a runtime bug

variables.name: --dx-cardview-card-min-width
variables.whenUnset: the theme minimum applies - a card may never get narrower than the theme allows

variables.name: --dx-cardview-card-max-width
variables.whenUnset: the declaration disappears and max-width keeps its initial value none - an invented limit would clip cards

variables.name: --dx-cardview-card-cover-max-height
variables.whenUnset: the cards container declares the theme default on itself and the runtime overrides it there

variables.name: --dx-cardview-card-cover-ratio
variables.whenUnset: the declaration disappears and the cover keeps its natural proportions - an invented ratio distorts the image more than none

variables.name: --dx-scheduler-animation-top
variables.whenUnset: the appointment form animates from the top edge
